Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and masses with thick, irregular (often described as "shaggy") margins, some of which appear to be cavitating. This radiographic appearance is highly characteristic of Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA), distinguishing it from other causes of nodules that typically have smooth margins or present primarily as ground-glass opacities.
